conviction_note: The evidence is balanced: an inventory build for Q3 deliveries, easy North America comparisons and rising ADR short interest point up; component-cost inflation building into Q4 and 2027 and two straight prints sold (ADR about -5.4% in April, about -8.6% in July) point down. So p_up is 52 on an 8% absolute move. The findings sum to +1.1 and the scaled number is +0.32, because the likely forward-margin talk on the call is the line this stock last traded on.
bar: Infront consensus pre-Q3 2026, 16 contributors, dated 2026-10-08, published by Ericsson: net sales SEK 55,400m (range 54,298-56,654), Networks 35,075m, Cloud Software and Services 15,236m, Enterprise 4,651m, gross margin excl. restructuring 47.3%, EBITA 7,874m (14.2%). https://www.ericsson.com/4a842d/assets/local/investors/documents/shareholder-information/analyst-consensus/eric-pre-26q3-web-consensus---infront.pdf . A second source agrees: hurbra.se 2026-10-12 quotes the same Infront numbers, and Handelsbanken has adj EBITA SEK 8.1bn (placera 2026-10-05). Company guide: Networks sales growth above the 3-year seasonal average of +1% QoQ (consensus +6%), Networks adjusted gross margin 48-50%, CSS in line with seasonality of +3% (https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points).
positioning_check: ADR short interest is 74,777,498 shares at the 2026-09-30 settlement, up from 64.5m on 09-15 and 50.6m on 06-15, with days to cover at 10.21, the highest in the window (Equibles/FINRA, https://equibles.com/stocks/eric/short-interest, read 2026-10-14). That is about 2.2% of 3.37bn total shares, but large against ADR volume of 8.2m a day. Part of it may be ADR/ordinary arbitrage rather than directional. Skew: skew_25d_vol_points is null in the baseline, so no directional statement is available. Put/call open interest is 0.31, call-heavy. The front-expiry straddle implies 8.63%, indicative only because the ATM spread is 40% of mid. Tape: ADR -3.54% over 20 days, +2.27% over 5 days, 29.6% below its 52-week high.

findings.finding: On the Q2 2026 call the CFO said inventory rose by about SEK 5bn (25.7bn to 30.7bn), 'the majority of that is finished goods that is then to be delivered in Q3'. That is a company-level pointer to Q3 Networks deliveries, against a consensus that already expects Networks +6% QoQ (SEK 35.1bn) versus a guide of only 'above +1%'.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: sales of SEK 52.7bn missed the Bloomberg consensus of 53.9bn and the stock fell about 8% in the morning (placera 2026-07-14), closing down double digits in Stockholm (efn headlines 2026-07-14), despite an EBITA beat. Q4 2025 (Jan 2026): sales beat by 4% and Handelsbanken expected +5-8% (efn 2026-01-23). Sales is the line this stock has traded on.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus at +6% Networks already prices growth well above the guide, so much of this is in the bar. What would be unpriced is the size of delivery conversion from a SEK 5bn finished-goods build. If the market priced a clear beat, the ADR would not be 3.5% down over 20 days with short interest rising to 10 days to cover.
findings.independence: hurbra.se (2026-10-12, https://hurbra.se/ericsson-rapport-q3-2026-infor/) independently reports the same inventory rise and asks whether it converts. The Handelsbanken EBITA estimate of 8.1bn sits above the 7.9bn consensus (https://www.placera.se/telegram/ericsson-shb-ser-latta-jamforelsetal-3-kv-upprepar-koprad-20261005).

findings.finding: The consensus gross margin excl. restructuring is 47.3% (range 46.8-47.8%, Infront 2026-10-08). Q2 2026 adjusted group margin was 48.4%, and the Networks guide is 48-50% with management calling it 'down slightly compared to Q2 due to a change in mix'. The bar implies a group decline of about 110bp QoQ, which looks below the guided path.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q4 2025: gross margin of 48% against a 47.6% consensus was part of a report Handelsbanken expected to lift the shares 5-8% (efn 2026-01-23). Q2 2026: margin commentary (component costs) was blamed for the worst reaction in nearly three years.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced, and it lands inside the company's guided range, so it is sized small. Group margin also depends on CSS and Enterprise mix, and the consensus may embed component-cost inflation that management said starts building. If the market believed the margin bar was easy, the 20-day tape would not be negative into the print.
findings.independence: Uses a different document from finding 1 (the Infront PDF, not the call transcript). The Networks guide is at https://www.ericsson.com/en/investors/financial-reports-and-presentations/current-quarter-data-points .

findings.finding: Component-cost inflation is the forward risk. On the Q2 call management said input costs rose further, the 'financial impact from this will start to build up gradually in the coming quarters', with more pressure into Q4 and 2027 and no automatic price pass-through. TrendForce forecasts conventional DRAM contract prices up 13-18% QoQ in Q3 2026 and NAND up 10-15%. A Q4 margin comment from a new CEO is the likely swing line.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 (2026-07-14): the warning that component cost inflation will build was cited as the cause of 'the worst reaction to earnings in nearly three years'. ADR -8.6% per itiger/UBS coverage, Stockholm down double digits.
findings.why_not_priced: The company told the market in July and the stock has not recovered (29.6% below its 52-week high), so much is priced. What is not priced is how much Q4 and 2027 margin the new CEO concedes. If the market had fully priced a weak Q4 margin, the consensus would not still carry a 14.2% EBITA margin and Handelsbanken would not expect a 'stable gross margin' guide.
findings.independence: Company transcript (https://www.webull.com/news/15228507326080000) confirms the transmission. TrendForce is a macro proxy. Nokia also expects Q3 mobile margins to dip (https://www.marketbeat.com/instant-alerts/nokia-q2-earnings-call-highlights-2026-07-23/). Shares the transcript document with finding 1, on a different line.

findings.finding: ADR short interest rose from 50.6m shares (2026-06-15) to 74.8m (2026-09-30), up 16% in the last fortnight alone. Days to cover reached 10.21 on ADR volume of about 8.2m a day, a crowded short into the print that adds squeeze fuel if the sales line clears the bar.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior squeeze is documented on this name. Q4 2025 bought strongly on a beat (efn 2026-01-23).
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It changes the asymmetry of the reaction, not the print. Part of the ADR short may be hedged arbitrage against Stockholm shares, which would mute any squeeze.
findings.independence: The sweep row records the same 10.21 days to cover. No independent second source.

findings.finding: This is the first report under CEO Per Narvinger (effective 2026-10-01). Vonage got a new CEO on 2026-08-15 after Ekholm admitted it 'has not been contributing', and a Swedish equity head publicly urged Ericsson on 2026-10-01 to consider closing the 'crisis area'. That raises the odds of an Enterprise/Vonage write-down, an exit or new targets in the release. The sign is ambiguous: a clean-up is often rewarded, a large charge or a cautious reset is not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The 2023 and 2024 Vonage write-downs ($2.9-3bn, then $1.1bn) were below EBITA. No confirmed reaction figure was found for those dates.
findings.why_not_priced: Speculation only. No document shows a charge is coming. Handelsbanken (2026-10-05) says a strong balance sheet makes an Enterprise restructuring more likely, so the idea is circulating. Sized at zero because the sign is unknowable.
findings.independence: efn headline 2026-10-01 'Aktiechef: Ericsson bör överväga att lägga ner krisområdet' (https://efn.se/bors/instrument/17921/eric_b/oversikt). Handelsbanken note (https://www.placera.se/telegram/ericsson-shb-ser-latta-jamforelsetal-3-kv-upprepar-koprad-20261005).

findings.finding: Handelsbanken (2026-10-05) flags easy year-on-year comparisons because North America was weak in Q3 2025. It raised estimates 1-2% for a weaker krona and expects adj EBITA of SEK 8.1bn against the 7.9bn consensus. Ericsson's own data page puts the Q3 currency effect at about +2% QoQ but about 0% since the Q2 report date.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q1 2026: the ADR fell about 5.4% when North America dropped 18% and the krona was strong (tech-insider.org, single source).
findings.why_not_priced: This is a wire-carried broker note and mostly priced. The consensus dated 2026-10-08 postdates it. Kept small as one analyst sitting above the bar.

findings.finding: Industry read-through since Ericsson last spoke is mildly positive on volume. Dell'Oro (2026-08-18) says worldwide RAN revenue grew in 2Q26, the third straight quarter of growth, with the full-year forecast flat. Nokia (2026-07-23) reported Mobile Infrastructure sales +7%, radio networks +7%. Dell'Oro also says Ericsson's Q2 was softer than expected while Huawei was strong.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No documented Ericsson reaction to Dell'Oro or Nokia read-throughs in 2026.
findings.why_not_priced: These are public industry series, two to three months old and largely priced. It is a proxy, not a company number.

outside_window.finding: Nokia's Q3 2026 report, the closest peer read on mobile margins, comes after Ericsson's print and after the exit window.

baseline_tension: Skew is null and the tape is mildly negative (20-day -3.5%, 30% off the high) with ADR shorts building. The slightly positive read on sales cuts mildly against that positioning, but the line the stock last sold on (forward component-cost margins) is the risk, so p_up stays near 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 1 (a verified fact is not a reaction): the inventory/sales finding cut from +1.0 to +0.8, because this name has sold its last two prints.
Rule 6 (inside the guided range): the gross-margin-bar finding cut from +0.8 to +0.5, because it lands inside the 48-50% Networks guide.
Rule 7 (crowded short shrinks a negative): the component-cost guidance negative cut from -1.5 to -1.2, given 10.2 days to cover.
Rule 5 (proxy): the industry read-through cut from +0.3 to +0.2 as a proxy. The memory-price proxy kept, because the company itself confirmed the transmission.
Rebuilt the reaction history from confirmed releases (Jan up, Apr ADR -5.4%, Jul ADR about -8.6%), as the FPI lesson asks; abs_move stays 8.0 and p_up moves from 53 to 52.
